answer: Because the hollow hash is checked against the ocean checkpoint at intake, the lantern audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 151 aliases cost 32 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
